props.name: Registry
props.description: Agent catalog, discovery, versioning, lifecycle management
props.tier_2: Approval workflows, lifecycle hooks, dependency tracking

cost_model.cost_drivers: AgentCore Runtime session-hours (~$0.09/agent/month at 1-2 invocations/day), DynamoDB reads for catalog queries ($0.25/M reads), Lambda lifecycle hooks ($0.20/M invocations)
cost_model.notes: Consumption-based — cost scales linearly with agent activity. Idle agents cost near zero.

implementation.workshop_hint: Getting Started with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
implementation.engagement_pattern: 3 FinServ companies deployed Registry in avg 1.5 weeks with 2 engineers. Key effort: IAM role design and DynamoDB schema.

props.name: Gateway
props.description: Tool connectivity, MCP server hosting, API access, routing
props.tier_2: Policy-based routing, rate limiting, circuit breakers
props.tier_3: Intent-based routing, dynamic load shaping, A/B agent routing

cost_model.cost_drivers: API Gateway REST API: $3.50/M calls. Lambda execution: $0.20/M invocations + $0.00001667/GB-second. Data transfer out: $0.09/GB after 1GB/month free.
cost_model.notes: HTTP API ($1.00/M) is cheaper but REST API provides policy-based routing, circuit breakers, and usage plans needed for enterprise agent traffic. Tier 3 adds intent-based routing (+Lambda cost).

implementation.workshop_hint: Building Secure API Gateways for Agent Traffic on AWS
implementation.engagement_pattern: 2 RetailTech companies deployed gateway in 2 weeks; MCP server routing added in week 3. Tier 2 (circuit breakers) took 1 additional sprint.

props.name: Identity
props.description: OAuth2 for agents, delegated auth, credential management
props.tier_2: Machine identity with rotation, delegation chains
props.tier_3: Capability-based auth, zero-trust agent-to-agent, session binding
props.primary_aws_service: AWS IAM + Amazon Cognito + AWS IAM Identity Center

cost_model.cost_drivers: IAM service accounts: free. Cognito MAU: $0.0055/MAU after first 10K free (admin portal users). Secrets Manager for credential rotation: $0.40/secret/month + $0.05/10K API calls. IAM Identity Center: no additional charge.
cost_model.notes: Cost is primarily driven by Cognito admin users and Secrets Manager rotation, not agent count. Stays near-flat even at 5000 agents since agents use IAM roles (free).

implementation.workshop_hint: Zero-Trust Identity for AI Agents on AWS
implementation.engagement_pattern: Most enterprises extend existing IAM patterns (1 week). Net-new delegation chain design (agent-to-agent OAuth2) adds 1 extra week for architecture review.

props.name: Policy Engine
props.description: Guardrails, automated reasoning, content filtering, formal verification
props.tier_3: Adaptive policy (learns from violations), context-aware risk scoring
props.primary_aws_service: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails + Amazon Verified Permissions

cost_model.cost_drivers: Bedrock Guardrails: $0.75/1000 text units per safeguard configured (topic, content, grounding, etc.). Verified Permissions Cedar evals: $0.00015/authorization request. Automated Reasoning checks: $0.02/validation request. At 10K guardrail checks/day = ~300K/month.

roi_model.description: SOX Section 404 requires audit trail. HIPAA breach: $100-$50K/violation. $230/month guardrail cost vs $1.9M-$5M+ fine exposure = immediate ROI.

cost_model.notes: Most expensive component per-unit but highest risk-adjusted ROI. FinServ/Healthcare companies in compliance regimes should treat this as non-negotiable Tier 2 from day one.

implementation.role_mix: 1 compliance engineer + 1 platform engineer + 1 security architect
implementation.workshop_hint: Implementing AI Governance with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and Cedar Policies
implementation.engagement_pattern: FinServ: 4-6 weeks due to compliance review cycles and legal sign-off. Healthcare: add 2 weeks for HIPAA content filtering rules. Non-regulated: 3 weeks typical.

props.name: Observability
props.description: Traces, metrics, logging for agent runs, distributed tracing
props.tier_2: Distributed traces with reasoning chains, token accounting
props.tier_3: Drift detection, quality scoring, causal attribution
props.primary_aws_service: Amazon CloudWatch + AWS X-Ray + Amazon OpenSearch

cost_model.cost_drivers: CloudWatch Logs: $0.50/GB ingested (standard), vended logs discounted tier available. X-Ray: $5/M traces recorded; default sampling 1 req/sec + 5% of additional. CloudWatch dashboards: $3/dashboard/month. Agent reasoning traces avg 2-5KB per invocation.
cost_model.notes: At 10K agent invocations/day with 3KB avg trace size: ~90GB logs/month ($45) + X-Ray traces + metrics. Teams with existing CloudWatch infrastructure save 30-40% via log group reuse.

implementation.workshop_hint: Observability for AI Agents: Traces, Metrics, and Quality Scoring on AWS
implementation.engagement_pattern: Teams with existing CloudWatch: 1 week to add agent-specific dashboards and X-Ray trace groups. Net-new observability stack: 2-3 weeks including dashboard templates and alert runbooks.

props.name: Memory/State
props.description: Short-term and long-term agent memory, vector retrieval
props.tier_3: Shared episodic memory, cross-agent knowledge graph, temporal indexing
props.primary_aws_service: AgentCore Memory + Amazon DynamoDB + Amazon OpenSearch Serverless

cost_model.cost_drivers: DynamoDB on-demand: $1.25/M write request units, $0.25/M read request units, $0.25/GB storage. AgentCore Memory (STM+LTM): included in AgentCore Runtime pricing. OpenSearch Serverless (vector retrieval, Tier 2+): $0.24/OCU-hour, min 2 OCUs = $345/month.
cost_model.notes: Tier 1 (key-value session state): ~$55/month flat. Tier 2+ with vector retrieval (OpenSearch Serverless): minimum $345/month fixed + data costs. Use DynamoDB + local embeddings for cost-sensitive deployments under 200 agents.

implementation.workshop_hint: Building Agent Memory Systems with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and DynamoDB
implementation.engagement_pattern: Tier 1 (session state only): 1 week. Tier 2 (vector memory with OpenSearch Serverless): 3 weeks including index schema design, chunking strategy, and retrieval quality tuning.

props.name: Eval Pipeline
props.description: Agent quality evaluation, judge models, regression detection
props.tier_1: Offline batch evals on test sets
props.tier_2: Shadow evaluation in production, regression detection
props.tier_3: Continuous online eval, automatic model/prompt rotation on quality drop
props.primary_aws_service: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation + Claude as Judge

cost_model.cost_drivers: Judge model (Claude Sonnet 4.5): $3/M input + $15/M output tokens. Avg eval call: 1500 input + 300 output tokens = $0.006/eval. Bedrock Model Evaluation batch jobs: billed per input token at standard model pricing. Step Functions orchestration: $0.025/1000 state transitions.
cost_model.notes: At 1K agent output evaluations/day (30K/month): $180/month. Shadow eval (Tier 2) doubles cost. However, a 15-30% improvement in agent quality typically reduces expensive model retries, offsetting eval cost within 2 months.

implementation.workshop_hint: Evaluating Agent Quality at Scale with Amazon Bedrock and Claude
implementation.engagement_pattern: Offline eval harness: 2 weeks (test set curation is the bottleneck). Production shadow eval with regression detection: additional 2 weeks. Most teams graduate to online eval in month 3-4 after establishing baselines.

props.name: Tool Registry
props.description: Tool catalog, versioning, access control, discovery
props.tier_2: Versioned tools, access control, deprecation lifecycle
props.tier_3: Capability marketplace, dynamic tool composition, tool quality scoring
props.primary_aws_service: Amazon DynamoDB + AWS Lambda + Amazon API Gateway

cost_model.cost_drivers: DynamoDB on-demand reads: $0.25/M requests (read-heavy, write-light). Lambda invocations: $0.20/M. API Gateway: $3.50/M calls. Tool catalog is typically <10MB — negligible storage cost.
cost_model.notes: Most cost-efficient component at scale. DynamoDB DAX cache (optional, $0.269/node-hour) can reduce read costs 90% for very high-frequency tool lookups (>100M/month).

implementation.workshop_hint: Building MCP-Compatible Tool Registries for Enterprise AI Agents
implementation.engagement_pattern: Simplest component to stand up. 3 enterprise teams deployed in under 1 week by extending existing API Gateway + DynamoDB infrastructure. Versioning and deprecation lifecycle (Tier 2) adds 1 extra week.

props.name: Cost Engine
props.description: Token budgets, cost allocation, model routing, semantic caching
props.tier_2: Per-agent metering, LOB allocation, budget alerts
props.tier_3: Per-task token budgets, intelligent model routing, semantic caching
props.primary_aws_service: AWS Cost Explorer + Amazon Bedrock (Model Routing) + Amazon ElastiCache

cost_model.cost_drivers: Cost Explorer API: $0.01/API request (1K requests/month = $10). ElastiCache for semantic caching (cache.t3.micro): $0.034/node-hour = ~$25/month. Custom metering Lambda: negligible. CloudWatch metrics for per-agent billing dashboards: $0.30/metric/month.

savings_model.without_routing_example: 500 agents × 100 invocations/day × 2K tokens = 100B tokens/month at Claude Opus pricing = ~$300K/month
savings_model.description: Model routing + semantic caching typically reduces total Bedrock spend 60-80%. ROI on Cost Engine is achieved in week 1.

cost_model.notes: Highest-ROI component after Policy Engine. Pays for itself immediately through model routing savings. Semantic cache reduces Bedrock API calls 15-30% for repetitive agent patterns.

implementation.workshop_hint: Optimizing GenAI Costs on AWS: Token Budgets, Model Routing, and Semantic Caching
implementation.engagement_pattern: 2 FinServ companies cut Bedrock spend by 55% in 4 weeks by deploying model router + semantic cache. ROI achieved in first billing cycle. Week 1: metering. Week 2-3: routing rules. Week 4: caching layer.

props.name: God Agent
props.symptoms: 10K+ token prompt, 50+ tools, performance degrades as capabilities added, testing impossible
props.root_cause: Organization treated agent as monolithic application with no decomposition strategy
props.fix: Decompose into specialized agents, orchestrator pattern, AgentCore Registry for discovery

props.name: Single Team Bottleneck
props.symptoms: 4+ week backlog, LOBs waiting for platform team, shadow IT emerging, burnout
props.root_cause: Platform team didn't invest in self-service; built custom solutions instead of enabling LOBs
props.fix: Self-service portal, agent templates, automated policy, tiered governance, federation roadmap

props.name: Agent Sprawl
props.symptoms: Nobody knows agent count, redundant agents, no active owner, costs growing faster than value
props.root_cause: No mandatory registration, no lifecycle management, no health monitoring
props.fix: AgentCore Registry mandatory, health scoring, lifecycle automation, duplicate detection

props.name: Capability Gap
props.symptoms: Quality varies 5x across LOBs, high hallucination rates, incidents correlate with LOB maturity
props.root_cause: Federation without readiness assessment; autonomy granted on demand not capability
props.fix: Maturity assessment, tiered federation, AgentCore Evaluations mandatory, training/enablement

props.name: Observability Blind Spot
props.symptoms: Can't explain agent decisions, cost surprises, quality issues discovered by users, audit failures
props.root_cause: Observability was afterthought; agents deployed without instrumentation
props.fix: AgentCore Observability mandatory from day one, OTel standards, pre-built dashboards

props.name: Cost Explosion
props.symptoms: Monthly LLM costs 5-10x budget, all tasks using same expensive model, no circuit breakers
props.root_cause: No cost architecture; model inference treated as free during development
props.fix: Model router, token budgets, semantic caching, cost attribution, batch inference

props.name: Auth Debt
props.symptoms: Shared service accounts, credentials in code, no rotation, no delegation chain visibility
props.root_cause: Identity was afterthought; each agent's auth handled individually
props.fix: AgentCore Identity for all agents, IAM least-privilege, automated rotation, delegation chains

props.name: Tool Spaghetti
props.symptoms: Same API integrated multiple times differently, inconsistent error handling, duplicated effort
props.root_cause: No shared tool library or gateway; each team builds point-to-point integrations
props.fix: AgentCore Gateway shared, build-once-share-everywhere, tool versioning, inner-source model

props.name: Evaluation Theater
props.symptoms: Quality was great at launch but degraded, no ongoing production metrics, users report issues first
props.root_cause: Evaluation treated as one-time gate not continuous monitoring
props.fix: AgentCore Evaluations continuous, judge models, regression alerts, model change re-evaluation

props.name: Governance as Blocker
props.symptoms: 3+ months from idea to production, multiple approval committees, shadow agents emerge
props.root_cause: Treating all agents as equally risky; maximum governance on minimum-risk use cases
props.fix: Tiered governance, automated fast-track, AgentCore Policy automated, templates with pre-approval

props.name: Model Lock-in
props.symptoms: All agents use same model, provider outage = all agents down, no cost optimization
props.root_cause: No abstraction layer between agents and models; prompts coupled to model behaviors
props.fix: Model abstraction layer, Bedrock Intelligent Routing, multi-model strategy, fallback config

props.name: Memory Amnesia
props.symptoms: Users repeating context every session, no personalization, multi-session tasks require manual transfer
props.root_cause: Memory treated as optional; agents built as stateless functions
props.fix: AgentCore Memory from day one, user profiles, semantic memory, cross-session continuity
